newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Nationalists lose bid to ban TV debate.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Nationalists lose bid to ban TV debate.

text.p: The Scottish Nationalist Party (SNP) on Thursday lost a legal bid to prevent its exclusion from a proposed pre-election television debate between Britain's prime minister and main opposition leader.
The SNP had wanted its leader Alex Salmond to join Prime Minister John Major and Labour Party leader Tony Blair for the debate when it is transmitted in Scotland.
The nationalist party had asked Scotland's highest court to rule that television companies would be breaching their duty of impartiality by excluding Salmond.
A Court of Sessions judge ruled against the SNP, saying that broadcasters could use their own judgement about their programmes.
Broadcasting of election campaigns is tightly controlled in Britain, with no paid commercials and the planned debate is widely seen as a key moment in the campaign.
The SNP is Scotland's second largest political party after Labour, but is tiny in overall British terms with only four of the 651 MPs in the outgoing parliament.

The Liberal Democrats, Britain's third national party trailing far behind Labour and Major's Conservatives, have also threatened legal action if their leader, Paddy Ashdown, is not given a role in the head-to-head debates.

Both Major and Blair have agreed to the debates, but the format has yet to be finalised, largely because of the need to fulfil election rules guaranteeing all major parties equal air time during the campaign for the May 1 election.
